cards.back: ≥ 65 mmHg (normal 70–100)
cards.rationale: Below 65, vital organs (brain, kidneys) lose perfusion.

cards.back: Cultures → antibiotics → IV fluids → recheck lactate
cards.rationale: Draw cultures before antibiotics so the organism can be identified.

cards.back: Norepinephrine
cards.rationale: Given after adequate fluid resuscitation to restore MAP.

cards.back: Obstruction: kink, secretions (suction), biting, mucus plug
cards.rationale: Low-pressure alarm = disconnection or leak instead.

cards.front: Normal ICP + first positioning step for high ICP?
cards.back: 5–15 mmHg; elevate HOB ~30° and keep head midline
cards.rationale: Promotes venous drainage; avoid neck flexion and hip flexion.

cards.back: Refractory hypoxemia with bilateral infiltrates
cards.rationale: Low oxygen that doesn’t improve with supplemental O₂; needs PEEP.

cards.back: Pneumothorax
cards.rationale: Confirm placement with a chest X-ray before use.

cards.front: Earliest sign a patient is deteriorating?
cards.back: Change in level of consciousness / new restlessness
cards.rationale: Read the trend — rising HR/RR with falling BP = compensating shock.

cards.back: Epinephrine IM
cards.rationale: Antihistamines and steroids are adjuncts, not first-line.

cards.back: MONA — Morphine, Oxygen, Nitroglycerin, Aspirin (aspirin early) + ECG, keep at rest
cards.rationale: Never ambulate a client with possible cardiac chest pain.

cards.front: Before giving tPA for stroke, confirm…
cards.back: Exact symptom-onset time and rule out hemorrhage (CT)
cards.rationale: tPA is time-limited and contraindicated with bleeding/recent surgery.

cards.back: Tracheal deviation, absent breath sounds, hypotension → needle decompression
cards.rationale: Air trapped under pressure collapses the lung and shifts the mediastinum.
cards.hint: Trachea runs away from the bad side.

cards.front: First priority in a major burn?
cards.back: Airway (assess for inhalation injury), then fluid resuscitation (Parkland)
cards.rationale: Facial burns/soot/hoarseness signal impending airway loss.

cards.back: Tachycardia, hypotension, low urine output, cool/clammy, thirst
cards.rationale: Stop the loss, replace the volume — in that order.
cards.hint: Fast pulse, low pressure, low urine.

cards.back: The airway/breathing problem — unstable over stable, acute over chronic
cards.rationale: New shortness of breath with low SpO₂ beats pain or discharge tasks.

cards.back: N-acetylcysteine (NAC)
cards.rationale: Give early to prevent hepatic failure.

cards.front: Late decelerations mean… and first action?
cards.back: Uteroplacental insufficiency → stop oxytocin, turn to side, give O₂, IV fluids
cards.rationale: “Late is bad” — the fetus isn’t getting enough oxygen.

cards.back: Head compression — benign, mirror the contraction
cards.rationale: No action needed; contrast with late (placental) and variable (cord).

cards.front: #1 cause of early postpartum hemorrhage + first action?
cards.back: Uterine atony → massage the fundus
cards.rationale: A boggy fundus displaced upward/right suggests a full bladder — empty it next.

cards.back: Severe headache, visual changes, epigastric/RUQ pain
cards.rationale: These warn of impending eclampsia (seizure).

cards.back: Absent DTRs, respirations < 12, low urine output → give calcium gluconate
cards.rationale: Monitor reflexes, respirations, and output during the infusion.
Bradycardia/tachycardia or loss of variability is concerning.

cards.front: Purpose of betamethasone in preterm labor?
cards.back: Accelerates fetal lung maturity (surfactant)
cards.rationale: Given to mom, works on the baby’s lungs; tocolytics stop contractions.

cards.back: Yes — blue hands/feet with a pink trunk is normal in the first 24–48h
cards.rationale: Central cyanosis (lips/trunk) is never normal — that’s an emergency.
cards.hint: Blue ends okay, blue center not.
